queue.source: studio docs/research/reevo-teardown.md §8.2 (the voice memory: a rule the user says once and every draft obeys; one seller's pasted paragraph of no guessing, no AI language and no dashes plus a manual review step, which he said gets him to 80 to 85%) and §8.3 (a buyer: personalisation that goes rogue, every AI email using the same sales structure); MARKET-RESEARCH.md batch 1 (tone control asked for; the vendor's own remedy, write the emails as you would send them and give the tool that template; launching copy you then have to edit message by message without seeing why each hook was chosen), batch 2 (a copy tell, the human edit removed and brought back, template language bleeding into a personalised email), batch 3 (the edit is a right, not a prompt: change one word and keep the rest), batch 4 (personalisation that obeys the sender; the template is the tell) and Themes (copy nobody trusts, about twenty-five sightings).
queue.angle: For the founder whose first draft already comes from a tool. The buyers who use these tools name three failures: the copy has the same structure as everyone else's, personalisation fixes on a detail nobody would mention, and asking for one change rewrites the rest. Their own remedies are the method: write the first few emails yourself and hand them to the tool as the pattern; keep the standing rules in one place, said once and obeyed by every draft (no invented facts, the phrases you never use, the format you do use); read every draft before it sends, with the reason for its opening line beside it, and check for details carried over from another prospect; edit by hand, change the word and keep the sentence, and keep a tool that lets you; when you make the same correction three times, it is a new standing rule. The person still decides every sentence that sends, which keeps this consistent with cold-email-personalisation's third answer. Added 12 Oct 2026 by the weekly SEO pass. True or absent: the 80 to 85% is one seller's own estimate and is said as his; the "two words" subject-line claim is one buyer's report of unnamed research and stays out; the reply-rate and spam figures a batch 2 member quoted from a press article are unverified and stay out. Names no vendor, model, member or company. Publishes none of this product's own writing rules or prompts.

Leave agencies out with a written reason (too large for the fee to matter, the work is one service of four, paid per meeting so the work is not its cost, consulting first, turned into a vendor) and park the pages you cannot read. queue.source: studio docs/research/partner-types.md (The answer; Six partner types, ranked, for why each type's clients need the product and the recruiting verdict per type; What comparable tools pay, for the range and the benchmark average only; Recommendation, for the flat number, the hold, no cash bounty and the order) and consultant-message.md (the message's shape and Why it is shaped this way).
queue.angle: Recruit the people a client already pays to run their outbound, because they decide which tools the client uses and are judged on meetings booked; a referral from them arrives with the tool already chosen. Rank partner types by why their clients need what you sell, never by how many exist: done-for-you outbound agencies first, fractional sales leaders, consultants who build sales workflows, then CRM and RevOps implementers (slow, they expect a marketplace listing), coaches one at a time, white label after renewals. Pay one flat share inside the 20% to 35% comparable programmes pay, most for twelve months, with a 250-programme benchmark averaging 22% to 25%, and add a tier only when a partner with five paying clients asks. The commission is a tip: 20% of $999 a month is about $200 a month and $2,400 a year against a fractional sales leader's $8,000 to $12,000 monthly fee, so the partner buys the deliverable they can bill for. The message runs stake, claim, money, with one ask, one price, no feature list and a subject naming what the partner sells; shown as a generic template. Send to existing agencies first, then consultants, then fractional leaders through two or three communities. Added 22 Oct 2026 by the daily article. Names no vendor, platform, community, benchmark publisher, directory or person, carries no directory or commenter count, and states no price but our own ($999 a month, $9,990 a year) and our own published programme terms (20% for twelve months, a thirty-day hold).
